tasks.title: Add canFastForward(), rebaseContinue(), abortOnConflict to WorktreeManager
tasks.description: Add `canFastForward(projectPath, projectName, issueNumber, baseBranch)` using `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<baseBranch> mo/issue-N`. Add `abortOnConflict` option to existing `rebaseOntoMaster()` — when false, skip `git rebase --abort` on conflict, leaving markers in worktree. Ensure `rebaseContinue()` (rename from `continueRebase` if needed) exists and works with `GIT_EDITOR=true`. Return false on any error in canFastForward.
acceptanceCriteria: canFastForward() returns true when branch is linear descendant of baseBranch
canFastForward() returns false when branch has diverged
canFastForward() returns false when worktree/branch doesn't exist
rebaseOntoMaster({ abortOnConflict: false }) preserves conflict markers in worktree on conflict
rebaseOntoMaster({ abortOnConflict: true }) and default behavior aborts rebase on conflict
rebaseContinue() runs `git rebase --continue` with GIT_EDITOR=true and returns RebaseResult
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Existing continueRebase() at line 280 already does most of what rebaseContinue needs. The abortOnConflict option is additive — existing callers pass no options and get default true behavior.

tasks.title: Rewrite MergeQueue.processItem() with rebase-first single path
tasks.description: Rewrite processItem() to: (1) set state Rebasing, (2) call canFastForward — if true, skip rebase and go to FF merge, (3) if not FF, call rebaseOntoMaster({ abortOnConflict: false }), (4) on conflict: abort rebase, fetch fresh master (smartFetch), retry rebase once, (5) if retry still conflicts: set Resolving, call resolveConflicts delegate then rebaseContinue, (6) if resolveConflicts succeeds: FF merge via mergeBack, (7) build verify, (8) on success: Merged + cleanup, on failure: BuildFailed + rollback. Add `resolveConflicts` to MergeQueueDeps interface as `(entry: MergeEntry, worktreePath: string, conflictFiles: string[]) => Promise<{ success: boolean; error?: string }>`. Update recoverFromDB() to include MergeState.Resolving in active states query.
acceptanceCriteria: processItem checks canFastForward first — skips rebase when FF is possible
When not FF: rebaseOntoMaster called with { abortOnConflict: false }
On first rebase conflict: abort + smartFetch + retry rebase once
On retry conflict: sets Resolving, calls resolveConflicts delegate
resolveConflicts delegate returns { success: true } → rebaseContinue → FF merge → build verify → Merged
resolveConflicts returns { success: false } → abort rebase → Blocked
Build failure: rollback merge (git reset --hard HEAD~1) → BuildFailed
recoverFromDB includes MergeState.Resolving in findByMergeStates query, resets to Pending
MergeQueueDeps has resolveConflicts field
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: The resolveConflicts delegate keeps MergeQueue decoupled from agent runtime. Server will inject the actual implementation. MergeQueue only calls the delegate and handles its result.

tasks.title: Add conflict resolution events to EventBus and SSE
tasks.description: Add three new event types to EventMap in event-bus.ts: `agent_conflict_resolution_started` (payload: { issueId, projectId, issueNumber, conflictFiles }), `agent_conflict_resolution_completed` (payload: { issueId, projectId, issueNumber }), `agent_conflict_resolution_failed` (payload: { issueId, projectId, issueNumber, error }). Add these to ALL_EVENT_TYPES in api/events.ts. Add to event-formatter.ts for CLI display.
acceptanceCriteria: EventMap type includes agent_conflict_resolution_started with { issueId, projectId, issueNumber, conflictFiles }
EventMap type includes agent_conflict_resolution_completed with { issueId, projectId, issueNumber }
EventMap type includes agent_conflict_resolution_failed with { issueId, projectId, issueNumber, error }
ALL_EVENT_TYPES in api/events.ts includes all three new events
SSE clients receive these events when emitted

tasks.notes: These events are emitted by the resolveConflicts callback (T-004), not by MergeQueue itself. MergeQueue emits merge_started/merge_completed/merge_blocked/merge_failed as before.

tasks.title: Simplify agent_completed handler + implement resolveConflicts callback
tasks.description: Replace the 80-line agent_completed handler in server/index.ts (lines 161-243) with a simple call to mergeQueue.enqueue(projectId, issueNumber). Then implement the resolveConflicts callback: (1) emit agent_conflict_resolution_started, (2) create ACP connection with conflict resolution prompt listing conflict files, (3) call conn.prompt() and conn.close(), (4) on success: call worktreeManager.rebaseContinue(), emit agent_conflict_resolution_completed, return { success: true }, (5) on failure: emit agent_conflict_resolution_failed, return { success: false, error }. The callback is passed as resolveConflicts in the MergeQueue constructor deps. Use the existing buildConflictResolutionPrompt from workflow-controller for the prompt text.
acceptanceCriteria: agent_completed handler calls only mergeQueue.enqueue(projectId, issueNumber) — no direct mergeBack, no mergeMasterInWorktree, no pipeline re-entry
resolveConflicts callback creates ACP session with conflict resolution prompt
resolveConflicts emits agent_conflict_resolution_started before agent session
resolveConflicts calls rebaseContinue() after agent completes successfully
resolveConflicts emits agent_conflict_resolution_completed on success
resolveConflicts emits agent_conflict_resolution_failed on failure
resolveConflicts returns { success: boolean; error?: string }
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: The buildConflictResolutionPrompt function already exists in workflow-controller. Extract it to a shared location (e.g., agent/prompts.ts) so both WorkflowController and server can use it. The ACP session creation pattern (createAcpConnection + conn.prompt + conn.close) is the same as in runConflictResolutionStage.
